items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to alternative
fuel standards and specifications
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6850

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to alterna-
tive fuel standards and specifications

1.  
PURPOSE:

The purpose of the bill is to authorize the Commissioner of Agriculture
and Markets to promulgate regulations for non-petroleum liquid automo-
tive fuels, such as ethanol, butanol, methanol, and fuels derived from
biological materials, and to authorize sampling to ensure compliance
with the established standards. At present, such fuels are not being
offered for sale in the state but it is anticipated that they will be in
the near future and should be subject to similar regulation and testing
as provided for petroleum fuel.

2.  
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends AML section 179(3)(b) to authorize the
Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets to promulgate standards for
non-petroleum liquid automotive fuels. Section 2 of the bill amends AML
section 179(19Xa) to authorize the Commissioner to take and test samples
of liquid automotive fuel to determine adherence to applicable stand-
ards. Section 3 of the bill amends paragraphs (b) and (c) of AML section
179(19) to authorize the Commissioner to provide assistance to local
weights and measures directors so that they can determine whether liquid
automotive fuel, offered for sale within their jurisdiction, adheres to
applicable standards.

3.  
EXISTING LAW:

AML section 179 currently authorizes the Commissioner to promulgate
regulations setting for standards for, to take samples of, and to aid
local weights and measures directors in determining adherence to stand-
ards applicable to petroleum products.

4.  
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.

5.  
STATEMENT IN SUPPORT:

The proposed amendments to subdivisions (3) and (19) of AML section 179
would allow the Commissioner to set and enforce standards for non-petro-
leum automotive fuels. The use of alternative non-petroleum based auto-
motive fuels (e.g. biodiesel and fuel-ethanol) is expanding and, in
order to maintain a level playing field in the marketplace, these
products should be tested for quality. Consumers would be better served
by the establishment of minimum quality standards for alternative non-
petroleum-based fuels.

6.  
POSSIBLE OBJECTIONS:

The proposed amendments will authorize the Commissioner to promulgate
standards for liquid automotive fuels, and to take certain actions to
ensure that such standards are being complied with, to the benefit of
the industry and consumers alike; as such, no reasonable objections to
the amendments are anticipated.

7.  
OTHER STATE AGENCIES INTERESTED:

Department of State (Consumer Protection), Department of Environmental
Conservation, NYSERDA and Taxation and Finance

8.  
KNOWN POSITION OF OTHERS:

Unknown.

9.  
BUDGET IMPLICATIONS:

None.

10.  
LOCAL IMPACT:

This bill would not impose a mandate on a county, city, town, village,
school district or special district

summary: Authorizes the commissioner of agriculture and markets, in consultation with the commissioner of environmental conservation, to adopt rules and regulations setting forth standards relating to alternative fuel quality; authorizes the commissioner of agriculture and markets to inspect, test and take samples of alternative fuel kept, offered or exposed for sale or in the process of delivery or transport; defines the term "alternative fuel" means alcohols such as ethanol, methanol, butanol and non-petroleum liquid or gaseous fuels, other than alcohol, derived from biological materials; makes related provisions.
